input: s is a primitive string containing only ASCII decimal digits 0 through 9. The empty string is accepted as an explicit zero-result extension. Preconditions, including the paired numeric bounds, are not checked at runtime.
return: The Number integer count of ways to split s into tokens 1 through 26, representing letters A through Z. Tokens cannot have a leading zero: a zero contributes only as the second digit of 10 or 20. An empty string, a leading zero or a string with no valid complete split returns zero.
mutation_aliasing: Strings are immutable and only read. All rolling counts are local scalars. The result aliases no mutable input, and the Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: The paired domain bounds s.length by 4294967295 and requires the number of valid decodings of every prefix, not just the final string, to be <= 9007199254740991. The empty-prefix state is one. Each current sum counts a prefix and each retained state counts an earlier prefix, so all counts and additions stay within the safe-integer range; indices and loop increments do too. NaN, infinities and BigInt are not used. ASCII code-unit comparisons agree with the paired Python digit comparisons; no integer parsing or Unicode normalization is used.
complexity: O(s.length + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space under constant-cost string indexing and safe-integer arithmetic. At each index, oneBack counts the preceding prefix and twoBack counts the prefix before that. A nonzero single digit contributes oneBack; a valid 10..26 pair contributes twoBack. Shift both states only after forming the new prefix count; no recursion or substring copies are used.
